interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang prompting a student response, with a brief staff aside

speaker_notes.note: The microphone instruction is not a substantive audience question; it is room logistics preceding the first student answer.
ASR collapses the student's answer with light back-and-forth and a stray Q&A announcement, but the central argument about heaven as exclusion and stagnation remains recoverable.

claims.claim: Jiang deliberately starts the Divine Comedy course with Paradise rather than Inferno, promising that the rationale will become clear over time.
The course uses a public website as the shared reading interface and expects students to work directly from the displayed text.
One student defines heaven as fulfillment, peace, harmony, and a felt destination where negative emotions disappear and the best of the self remains.
Another student argues that heaven would be exclusionary and stagnant because different religions imagine irreconcilable paradises and perfection leaves no room for change.
Jiang says a purely logical answer to heaven misses the point of reading Dante, because intuition and imagination rather than analytic reason lead toward the deeper truth of the poem.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang begins the Divine Comedy from Paradise first, turning the usual reading order into part of the lesson itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we are actually start in part three
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It signals that the class will rearrange inherited reading habits in order to see Dante's architecture differently.

signature_moments.moment: A student's skeptical heaven-as-stagnation answer becomes Jiang's first contrast between logical cleverness and the imaginative mode Dante demands.
signature_moments.source_phrase: that's not the answer I want though
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the opening pedagogical turn of the series: Dante will be read through imaginative participation rather than detached analysis.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang says imagination leads to the true truth, not just exam-style reasoning.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the imagination is what will lead you to the true truth
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the course its epistemic key before substantive interpretation begins.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's preferred mode for entering Dante: a way of seeing that exceeds school-exam logic and reason.
The third part of the Divine Comedy, chosen here as the course's opening point rather than its endpoint.

chronology_notes.note: At the very start of the 2026-06-17 Dante series, Jiang sets the governing method: begin with Paradise and read by imagination rather than by purely analytic logic.

uncertainty_notes.note: ASR introduces obvious transcription noise in the book and translator names, but the structural claim about starting with Paradise and using the website is clear.
